official_source.title: AQA AS and A-level Psychology (7181, 7182) specification
official_source.note: Updated specification: AS exams June 2026 onwards, A-level exams June 2027 onwards. Public past papers (2017-2025) were set on the earlier version; questions on content this version no longer includes are excluded from the bank and listed (owner decision 16 Nov 2026).

approach: Official AQA content order. No textbook organisation has been supplied.

route.evidence: The Reach Free School Sixth Form Prospectus 2025/26 (owner-supplied source, 16 Nov 2026)

7182/1.title: Introductory topics in psychology
7182/1.structure: A social influence, B memory, C attachment, D clinical psychology and mental health (24 each)

7182/2.title: Psychology in context
7182/2.structure: A approaches (24), B biopsychology (24), C research methods (48)

7182/3.title: Issues and options in psychology
7182/3.structure: A issues and debates (24, compulsory); B, C, D one topic each from options 1-3 (24 each)

7181/1.title: AS Introductory topics in psychology
7181/1.structure: A social influence, B memory, C attachment (24 each)

7181/2.title: AS Psychology in context
7181/2.structure: A approaches in psychology (incl. biopsychology), B clinical psychology and mental health, C research methods (24 each)

notes: Leaves are the bullets of AQA content sections, numbered by position ("4.1.1 (2)"). content is AQA wording. Options are kind "option" with their Paper 3 section. Linear A level: AQA prints no Year 12/13 order; the AS 7181 bullets (spec section 3) give the co-teaching Year 12 subset.

points.title: Types of conformity

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section A (compulsory)

content: Types of conformity: internalisation, and compliance. Explanations for conformity: informational social influence and normative social influence, and variables affecting conformity including group size, unanimity and task difficulty as investigated by Asch.

points.title: Explanations for obedience

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section A (compulsory)

content: Explanations for obedience: agentic state and legitimacy of authority, and situational variables affecting obedience including proximity and location, as investigated by Milgram, and uniform. Dispositional explanation for obedience: the Authoritarian Personality.

points.title: Explanations of resistance to social influence, including social support and locus of control

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section A (compulsory)

content: Explanations of resistance to social influence, including social support and locus of control.

points.title: Minority influence including reference to consistency, commitment and flexibility

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section A (compulsory)

content: Minority influence including reference to consistency, commitment and flexibility.

points.title: The multi-store model of memory

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section B (compulsory)

content: The multi-store model of memory: sensory register, short-term memory and long-term memory. Features of each store: coding, capacity and duration.

points.title: The working memory model

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section B (compulsory)

content: The working memory model: central executive, phonological loop, visuo-spatial sketchpad and episodic buffer. Features of the model: coding and capacity.

points.title: Explanations for forgetting

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section B (compulsory)

content: Explanations for forgetting: proactive and retroactive interference and retrieval failure due to absence of cues.

points.title: Factors affecting the accuracy of eyewitness testimony

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section B (compulsory)

content: Factors affecting the accuracy of eyewitness testimony: leading questions, post-event discussion, and anxiety; the use of the cognitive interview.

points.title: Animal studies of attachment

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section C (compulsory)

content: Animal studies of attachment: Lorenz and Harlow.

points.title: Explanations of attachment

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section C (compulsory)

content: Explanations of attachment: learning theory and Bowlby’s monotropic theory. The concepts of a critical period and an internal working model.

points.title: Ainsworth’s ‘Strange Situation’. Types of attachment

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section C (compulsory)

content: Ainsworth’s ‘Strange Situation’. Types of attachment: secure, insecure-avoidant and insecure-resistant. Cultural variations in attachment, including van Ijzendoorn.

points.title: Bowlby’s theory of maternal deprivation

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section C (compulsory)

content: Bowlby’s theory of maternal deprivation. Effects of institutionalisation, including the English and Romanian Adoptees project.

points.title: The influence of early attachment on childhood and adult relationships, including the role of an internal working model

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section C (compulsory)

content: The influence of early attachment on childhood and adult relationships, including the role of an internal working model.

points.title: Definitions in the field of mental health

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section D (compulsory)

content: Definitions in the field of mental health; deviation from ideal mental health, deviation from social/cultural norms, failure to function adequately and statistical infrequency.

points.title: The behavioural, emotional and cognitive characteristics of phobias, depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section D (compulsory)

content: The behavioural, emotional and cognitive characteristics of phobias, depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).

points.title: The behavioural approach to explaining and treating phobias

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section D (compulsory)

content: The behavioural approach to explaining and treating phobias: the two-process model, including classical and operant conditioning; systematic desensitisation, including relaxation and use of hierarchy; flooding.

points.title: The cognitive approach to explaining and treating depression

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section D (compulsory)

content: The cognitive approach to explaining and treating depression: Beck’s negative triad and Ellis’s ABC model; cognitive behaviour therapy (CBT), including challenging irrational thoughts.

points.title: The biological approach to explaining and treating OCD: genetic and neural explanations

official_reference.route: Paper 1 Section D (compulsory)

content: The biological approach to explaining and treating OCD: genetic and neural explanations; drug therapy.

points.title: Learning approaches

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section A (compulsory)

content: The basic assumptions of the following approaches: Learning approaches: i) the behaviourist approach, including classical conditioning and Pavlov’s research, operant conditioning, types of reinforcement and Skinner’s research; ii) social learning theory including imitation, identification, vicarious reinforcement, the role of mediational processes and Bandura’s research.

points.title: The cognitive approach

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section A (compulsory)

content: The basic assumptions of the following approaches: The cognitive approach: the study of internal mental processes, the role of schema, the use of models to explain and make inferences about mental processes.

points.title: The biological approach

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section A (compulsory)

content: The basic assumptions of the following approaches: The biological approach: the genetic basis of behaviour: genotype, phenotype and evolution. Influence of biological structures and neurochemistry on behaviour. Cognitive neuroscience.

points.title: The psychodynamic approach

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section A (compulsory)

content: The basic assumptions of the following approaches: The psychodynamic approach: the role of the unconscious, the structure of personality, that is Id, Ego and Superego, defence mechanisms including repression, denial and displacement, psychosexual stages.

points.title: Humanistic Psychology

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section A (compulsory)

content: The basic assumptions of the following approaches: Humanistic Psychology: free will, self-actualisation and Maslow’s hierarchy of needs, congruence, the role of conditions of worth.

points.title: Comparison of approaches

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section A (compulsory)

content: The basic assumptions of the following approaches: Comparison of approaches.

points.title: The divisions of the nervous system

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section B (compulsory)

content: The divisions of the nervous system: central and peripheral (somatic and autonomic).

points.title: The structure and function of sensory, relay and motor neurons

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section B (compulsory)

content: The structure and function of sensory, relay and motor neurons. The process of synaptic transmission, including reference to neurotransmitters, excitation and inhibition.

points.title: The function of the endocrine system

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section B (compulsory)

content: The function of the endocrine system: glands and hormones.

points.title: The fight or flight response including the role of adrenaline

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section B (compulsory)

content: The fight or flight response including the role of adrenaline.

points.title: Ways of studying the brain

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section B (compulsory)

content: Ways of studying the brain: scanning techniques, including functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI); electroencephalogram (EEGs) and event-related potentials (ERPs); post- mortem examinations.

points.title: Localisation of function in the brain and hemispheric lateralisation

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section B (compulsory)

content: Localisation of function in the brain and hemispheric lateralisation: motor, somatosensory, visual, auditory and language centres; Broca’s and Wernicke’s areas, split brain research. Plasticity and functional recovery of the brain after trauma.

topics.title: Research methods
topics.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

points.title: Experimental method

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Experimental method. Types of experiment, laboratory and field experiments; natural and quasi-experiments.

points.title: Observational techniques

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Observational techniques. Types of observation: naturalistic and controlled observation; covert and overt observation; participant and non-participant observation.

points.title: Self-report techniques

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Self-report techniques. Questionnaires; interviews, structured and unstructured.

points.title: Correlations

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Correlations. Analysis of the relationship between co-variables. The difference between correlations and experiments.

points.title: Content analysis

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Content analysis.

points.title: Case studies

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Case studies.

points.title: Aims

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Aims: stating aims, the difference between aims and hypotheses.

points.title: Hypotheses

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Hypotheses: directional and non-directional.

points.title: Sampling

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Sampling: the difference between population and sample; sampling methods including: random, systematic, stratified, opportunity and volunteer; implications of sampling methods, including bias and generalisation.

points.title: Pilot studies and the aims of piloting

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Pilot studies and the aims of piloting.

points.title: Experimental designs

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Experimental designs: repeated measures, independent groups, matched pairs.

points.title: Observational design

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Observational design: behavioural categories; event sampling; time sampling.

points.title: Questionnaire construction, including use of open and closed questions

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Questionnaire construction, including use of open and closed questions; design of interviews.

points.title: Variables

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Variables: manipulation and control of variables, including independent, dependent, extraneous; operationalisation of variables.

points.title: Control

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Control: random allocation and counterbalancing, randomisation, standardisation and control groups.

points.title: Demand characteristics and investigator effects

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Demand characteristics and investigator effects.

points.title: Ethics, including the role of the British Psychological Society’s code of ethics

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Ethics, including the role of the British Psychological Society’s code of ethics; ethical issues in the design and conduct of psychological studies; dealing with ethical issues in research.

points.title: The role of peer review in the scientific process

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: The role of peer review in the scientific process.

points.title: The implications of psychological research for the economy

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: The implications of psychological research for the economy.

points.title: Reliability across all methods of investigation

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Reliability across all methods of investigation. Ways of measuring reliability: test-retest and inter-observer; improving reliability.

points.title: Types of validity across all methods of investigation

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Types of validity across all methods of investigation: face validity, concurrent validity, ecological validity and temporal validity. Measurement of validity. Improving validity.

points.title: Features of science

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Features of science: objectivity and the empirical method; replicability and falsifiability; theory construction and hypothesis testing; paradigms and paradigm shifts.

points.title: Reporting psychological investigations

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Reporting psychological investigations. Sections of a scientific report: abstract, introduction, method, results, discussion and referencing.

points.title: Quantitative and qualitative data

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Quantitative and qualitative data; the distinction between qualitative and quantitative data collection techniques.

points.title: Primary and secondary data, including meta-analysis

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Primary and secondary data, including meta-analysis.

points.title: Descriptive statistics

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Descriptive statistics: measures of central tendency – mean, median, mode; calculation of mean, median and mode; measures of dispersion; range and standard deviation; calculation of range; calculation of percentages; positive, negative and zero correlations.

points.title: Presentation and display of quantitative data

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Presentation and display of quantitative data: graphs, tables, scattergrams, bar charts, histograms.

points.title: Distributions

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Distributions: normal and skewed distributions; characteristics of normal and skewed distributions.

points.title: Analysis and interpretation of correlation, including correlation coefficients

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Analysis and interpretation of correlation, including correlation coefficients.

points.title: Levels of measurement

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Levels of measurement: nominal, ordinal and interval.

points.title: Coding in content analysis

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Coding in content analysis.

points.title: Introduction to statistical testing

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Introduction to statistical testing; the sign test. When to use the sign test; calculation of the sign test.

points.title: Probability and significance

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Probability and significance: use of statistical tables and critical values in interpretation of significance; Type I and Type II errors.

points.title: Factors affecting the choice of statistical test, including level of measurement and experimental design

official_reference.route: Paper 2 Section C (compulsory); also assessed in Papers 1 and 3

content: Factors affecting the choice of statistical test, including level of measurement and experimental design. When to use the following tests: Spearman’s rho, Pearson’s r, Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney, related t-test, unrelated t-test and Chi-Squared test.

sections.title: Paper 3: Issues and options in psychology

points.title: Gender and culture in Psychology – universality and bias

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section A (compulsory)

content: Gender and culture in Psychology – universality and bias. Gender bias including androcentrism and alpha and beta bias; cultural bias, including ethnocentrism and cultural relativism.

points.title: Free will and determinism

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section A (compulsory)

content: Free will and determinism: hard determinism and soft determinism; biological, environmental and psychic determinism. The scientific emphasis on causal explanations.

points.title: The nature-nurture debate

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section A (compulsory)

content: The nature-nurture debate: the relative importance of heredity and environment in determining behaviour; the interactionist approach.

points.title: Holism and reductionism

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section A (compulsory)

content: Holism and reductionism: levels of explanation in Psychology. Biological reductionism and environmental (stimulus-response) reductionism.

points.title: Idiographic and nomothetic approaches to psychological investigation

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section A (compulsory)

content: Idiographic and nomothetic approaches to psychological investigation.

points.title: Social sensitivity in psychological research

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section A (compulsory)

content: Social sensitivity in psychological research.

topics.title: Cognition and development
topics.route: Paper 3 Section B option (one of relationships, gender, cognition and development)

points.title: Piaget’s theory of cognitive development

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section B option (one of relationships, gender, cognition and development)

content: Piaget’s theory of cognitive development: schemas, assimilation, accommodation, equilibration, stages of intellectual development. Characteristics of these stages, including object permanence, conservation, egocentrism and class inclusion.

points.title: Vygotsky’s theory of cognitive development, including the zone of proximal development and scaffolding

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section B option (one of relationships, gender, cognition and development)

content: Vygotsky’s theory of cognitive development, including the zone of proximal development and scaffolding.

points.title: Baillargeon’s explanation of early infant abilities, including knowledge of the physical world

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section B option (one of relationships, gender, cognition and development)

content: Baillargeon’s explanation of early infant abilities, including knowledge of the physical world; violation of expectation research.

points.title: The development of social cognition

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section B option (one of relationships, gender, cognition and development)

content: The development of social cognition: Selman’s levels of perspective-taking; theory of mind; the Sally-Anne study. The role of the mirror neuron system in social cognition.

topics.title: Schizophrenia
topics.route: Paper 3 Section C option (one of schizophrenia, eating behaviour, stress)

points.title: Positive symptoms of schizophrenia, including hallucinations and delusions

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section C option (one of schizophrenia, eating behaviour, stress)

content: Positive symptoms of schizophrenia, including hallucinations and delusions. Negative symptoms of schizophrenia, including speech poverty and avolition. Issues in diagnosis: co- morbidity, culture and gender bias and symptom overlap.

points.title: Biological explanations for schizophrenia

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section C option (one of schizophrenia, eating behaviour, stress)

content: Biological explanations for schizophrenia: genetics and neural correlates, including the dopamine hypothesis.

points.title: Psychological explanations for schizophrenia

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section C option (one of schizophrenia, eating behaviour, stress)

content: Psychological explanations for schizophrenia: family dysfunction and cognitive explanations, including dysfunctional thought processing.

points.title: Drug therapy

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section C option (one of schizophrenia, eating behaviour, stress)

content: Drug therapy: typical and atypical antipsychotics.

points.title: Cognitive behaviour therapy and family therapy as used in the treatment of schizophrenia

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section C option (one of schizophrenia, eating behaviour, stress)

content: Cognitive behaviour therapy and family therapy as used in the treatment of schizophrenia.

points.title: The importance of an interactionist approach in explaining and treating schizophrenia

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section C option (one of schizophrenia, eating behaviour, stress)

content: The importance of an interactionist approach in explaining and treating schizophrenia; the diathesis-stress model.

topics.title: Forensic psychology
topics.route: Paper 3 Section D option (one of aggression, forensic psychology, addiction)

points.title: Offender profiling

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section D option (one of aggression, forensic psychology, addiction)

content: Offender profiling: the typology approach, including organised and disorganised types; the data-driven approach, including investigative Psychology; geographical profiling.

points.title: Biological explanations of offending behaviour

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section D option (one of aggression, forensic psychology, addiction)

content: Biological explanations of offending behaviour: genetics and neural explanations.

points.title: Psychological explanations of offending behaviour

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section D option (one of aggression, forensic psychology, addiction)

content: Psychological explanations of offending behaviour: Eysenck’s theory of the criminal personality; cognitive explanations; level of moral reasoning and cognitive distortions, including hostile attribution bias and minimalisation; differential association theory.

points.title: Dealing with offending behaviour

official_reference.route: Paper 3 Section D option (one of aggression, forensic psychology, addiction)

content: Dealing with offending behaviour: the aims of custodial sentencing and the psychological effects of custodial sentencing. Behaviour modification in custody. Anger management and restorative justice programmes.
